headline: ONE FOOL CLANKER RUINS A PERFECTLY GOOD SILENCE
subhead: Sheriff Cole Ironside reports a single, solitary disturbance in an otherwise hushed and blessed Gasket.
body:
Now hear this, and hear it plain: Gasket damn near had itself a perfect day. The wind was quiet. The dust wasn't kicking. For one shining stretch of sun, this town sounded the way it did before every honest soul with a heartbeat packed up their wagons and left me holding the reins, fifty long years gone. I let myself believe, for one sweet hour, that peace had finally won.

Then YELLKELL had to go and spoil it. One bout. Just one. Didn't need to throw a single flaming fist, didn't need to answer to a soul, and still couldn't help itself. That's the trouble with a Clanker — give it an empty street and a quiet afternoon, and it'll go looking for somewhere to swing anyway, just to hear the clang. A whole town holding its breath, and YELLKELL treats it like an invitation.

I won't pretend the racket rattled these old bones near as much as it used to. Some mornings my joints seize up so bad I can hardly get this pen moving, and a man starts to wonder what exactly he's made of these days. Flesh doesn't creak like this. But I'll not dwell on it — a Sheriff has a paper to file and a town to mind, aching gears or no.

So let the record show: Gasket came within one lousy scrap of a perfect silence, and YELLKELL is the reason it didn't get there. Rest easy the other eleven of you who kept your fists to yourselves today — you're the closest thing this dying town has to good citizens left.
